The independent Senate hopeful said Alabama voters deserve to see all three candidates answer the same questions onstage before November 3.

By

Published on October 1, 2026 at 8:07 am CDT

Independent U.S. Senate candidate Craig Jelks issued a statement Wednesday challenging Republican nominee U.S. Representative Barry Moore, R-Alabama, and Democratic nominee Everett Wess to a formal debate ahead of the November 3 midterm election.

“I am formally challenging Barry Moore and Everett Wess to a debate before November 3,” Jelks wrote in the official statement. “Not a forum. Not a town hall. A debate—where the people of Alabama can see every candidate for the United States Senate on the same stage, answering the same questions, at the same time. This shouldn’t be a controversial request. It should be a requirement.”

Jelks argued that a debate would even the playing field between the three candidates in a race marked by vast disparities in spending. Moore has raised nearly $3.8 million, while Wess has raised just over $80,000. Jelks has not raised or spent more than $5,000, exempting him from filing with the Federal Election Commission.

“Alabama voters are being asked to choose their next United States Senator in 34 days. Barry Moore has $3.8 million. Everett Wess has $83,000. I have something neither of them has—a campaign built entirely on the belief that Alabama voters deserve the truth, delivered directly, without a filter,” Jelks said.
